repairs.Harold Rogers:
Low household earnings define Kentucky's 5th: the median is $46,664, while its $121,100 middle home remains inexpensive beside that pay. Poverty is widespread, and unemployment is also elevated. Ownership is still common, so the low cost of housing supports buying even where incomes are limited. Only 62.7 people occupy each square mile, giving the seat a distinctly rural settlement pattern.

Credit unions account for 9.4 percent of retail deposit-taking offices, leaving them with an unusually small position beside banks. Y-12, L & N, and Members Choice provide the principal credit union names. Their employment intensity and office density both fall far short of the national norm, with neither materially ahead of the other. Community Trust Bank has the leading deposit total attached to local addresses, but federal booking practices make that label different from customer reach, and many banks operate here.

Measured in 2023, the job mix depended heavily on health care and social assistance, the largest field, plus retail trade. Mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction held the sharpest concentration versus the nation, although its share of employment was small. Utilities also had a heavier local presence than elsewhere. Finance and insurance remained comparatively thin. Extraction and care work therefore give the local economy its strongest distinction, while financial activity occupies a supporting position.
repairs.Pat Harrigan:
Joblessness is the clearest demographic distinction in North Carolina's 10th, holding at 3.0 percent. Its 787,565 residents otherwise occupy mixed economic ground: median household earnings are $71,999, the middle home is worth $309,200, and poverty is elevated beside peer seats. Owner occupancy and the weight of housing costs stay near ordinary national levels. The result is a place with plentiful work but less uniform household security.

Local credit union staffing reaches 1.59 times the national concentration, while office density is much closer to ordinary. That imbalance means the institutions employ more people than their physical network alone would predict. State Employees', Allegacy, and Truliant are prominent; collectively credit unions command 27.0 percent of retail banking locations. Truist Bank carries the foremost locally booked deposit total, one participant in a competitive bank field. Credit unions therefore have meaningful local scale without dominating the storefront market.

In the 2023 employment picture, manufacturing supplied the most distinctive concentration. Management of companies and enterprises was another unusually common line of work. Health care and social assistance joined retail trade as large job fields, while finance and insurance remained near its national baseline. The combined finance sector nonetheless expanded faster locally during the preceding decade. Mortgage originations focused primarily on purchases, another practical tie between household needs and local lenders.
repairs.Tom Barrett:
Pay stretches relatively far into homeownership here. A middle-priced home equals 3.5 times middle household earnings, while the income figure is 80,268 dollars and 73.2 percent of homes are owner occupied. About 792,585 people live across a district with moderate settlement density. These measures describe a stable ownership market rather than a place where shelter runs away from earnings. The combination gives households a comparatively attainable route from income to property.

Retail banking has a large cooperative component: credit unions operate 38.2 percent of its offices. MSU Federal, Lake Trust, and LaFCU supply the principal names. First National Bank of America has the foremost deposit amount assigned locally, though numerous banks maintain competing operations. Credit union staffing is much more concentrated than its already substantial office network. For households whose earnings align reasonably with home prices, those institutions function as a familiar part of the financial market rather than a minor alternative.

The employment snapshot dates to 2021. Public administration was heavily concentrated, with finance and insurance plus educational services also somewhat more common than their national baselines. Health care and social assistance joined retail trade among the main job fields. Approximately 305,900 positions made up the measured economy. Finance's modest specialization fit a place that also gave credit unions a substantial role in everyday financial service.
repairs.William Timmons:

Manufacturing remains the defining difference in the local job mix.
repairs.George Latimer:
Few places in this country pack people in as closely as this district does, and that crowding runs through everything else here. Households earn a median $102,025, well above most other districts, but housing runs expensive too, with a median house price of $671,100 against that income marking a ratio of 6.6. Homeownership sits at just 54.2 percent, a mark of a place built more around renters than owners. Unemployment runs a touch higher than in peer seats, even as poverty stays lower.

Credit unions hold just 13.0 percent of retail locations here, a thin slice next to nearly every comparable district, leaving deposit business concentrated among banks. Quorum, USAlliance, and Municipal carry that thin share locally. Morgan Stanley Private Bank leads the district on the deposit measure, a figure shaped by which office a bank books its deposits to rather than by how many branches it runs nearby, and it sits alongside many competing banks in the area. Credit union staffing and location footprint both run well under the countrywide baseline here, tracking each other closely.

In 2023, the seat's job mix relied hardest on real estate and rental and leasing, its most specialized sector by a wide margin against the countrywide baseline. Management of companies and other services added further specialization on top of that. Health care, retail, and related sectors employed the most people day to day. Mortgage lending here skewed heavily toward home purchases, 65.4 percent of originations, with only a small share reaching lower-income neighborhoods.
repairs.Gwen Moore:

Landmark, Educators, and UW Credit Union anchor that location footprint, which holds 22.5 percent of the retail branch market. U.S. Bank National Association books the leading deposit position in federal records, one name among many banks competing here. In 2023, the seat's job mix depended most on management of companies and enterprises, more than two and a half times the countrywide baseline. Health care and social assistance employed the most people outright, nearly a fifth of all jobs, well ahead of manufacturing and other large employers. Finance and insurance jobs ran far beyond the countrywide baseline too, a real cluster in a district otherwise built on services. Mortgage lending leaned toward home purchases over refinancing, with lower-income neighborhoods capturing a real share of that activity.
repairs.Kat Cammack:
